name: Major cyber incidents
summary: Refrigeration-control attacks hit shops across Europe and French blood banks; US agencies issued a warning on 5 Nov
state: Attacks on refrigeration controls hit stores in Belgium, Luxembourg and Sweden in a second wave, with later reports from Finland, Ireland, Estonia and the Netherlands (Help Net Security). France's blood service confirmed on 3 Nov that cold rooms were affected through a supplier, with no products lost (The Register). Five US agencies warned on 5 Nov of attacks on these systems, naming no culprit. GreyNoise first saw an OpenSSH authentication bypass exploited on 7 Nov, on a limited scale. No national-scale attack on power, health or finance had been found as of 9 Nov.
for_you: Food retailers, cold-storage operators and health services using connected refrigeration are most exposed. Organisations can follow NCSC guidance and the joint CISA and FBI advisory; administrators can check vendor advisories for OpenSSH.
rubric_hit: Attacks disrupting critical services and large retailers (European cold-chain attacks; US advisory 5 Nov): Watch. No national-scale attack found.
